column2: Nutmeg with camphor and sandal — the three cooling ones; yellow, white-colored, and likewise white, Bhargava,
black and red — one should declare the five colors. Water lily and lotus kinds are the three cool ones in worship of Hari;
saffron, red lotuses, and the red water lily — the three reds. Having worshipped Vishnu with incense, lamps and the rest, there is peace for men.
In a square pit of a cubit, eight or sixteen Brahmins; a lakh oblation or crore oblation with sesame, ghee, barley and grains;
having worshipped the planets with the Gayatri, all peace follows in order.
There, having set up Indra's banner, one should worship Shachi and Indra. On the eighth with sound of instruments one should bring that pole in;
on the eleventh fasting; on the twelfth the raised banner — one should worship, wrapped in cloth and the like, the lord of gods and Shachi in a pot:
Having worshipped Indra with the mantra, one who has conquered the earth would obtain heaven. Having drawn Bhadrakali on cloth one should worship her in Ashvina for victory,
on the eighth of the bright half likewise: weapon, bow, banner, umbrella, royal insignia, arms and the rest with flowers and the like.
Awake at night one should give an offering; on the second day one should worship again: "Bhadrakali, Mahakali, Durga, remover of difficulties,
Chandi, victor of the three worlds, be for my peace and victory." I shall tell the rule of the lustration (nirajana): one should proceed to the temple in the northeast;
there, having three arches, one should always worship the gods in the house. When the sun, leaving Chitra, reaches Svati,
from then on it should be done as long as the sun stays in Svati. Brahma, Vishnu, Shambhu, Indra, Fire and Wind,
Vinayaka, Kumara, Varuna, Kubera, Yama, Vishvedevas, Vaishravasa and the eight elephants — one should worship them:
Kumuda, Airavata, Padma, Pushpadanta, Vamana, Supratika, Anjana, Nila — worship should be made in the house and the rest.
The priest should offer ghee, fuel sticks, mustard seed and sesame; the eight pots, worshipped, with them the best horses and elephants should be bathed;
horses should be bathed and given pindas; but elephants first. One should lead them out through the arches, not crossing the city-gate and the like.
Then all should march; one should worship the royal insignia in the house; having worshipped Varuna in the west, at night one should give the offering to beings.
When the sun has gone to Vishakha the king should dwell in the hermitage; on that day he should adorn the vehicle especially;
worshipped royal insignia should be carried by men: elephant, horse, umbrella, sword, bow, drum,
banner and flag — the knower of dharma, knowing the time, should consecrate. Having consecrated them, he should then have all placed on elephant-backs;
the astrologer and the priest should be on the elephant; having mounted the consecrated ones he should go out by the arch;
having gone out, having mounted the elephant, he should then go out by the arch; having divided the offering by rule, the king on the elephant's back,
the heap of torches lighting the quarters, the king should circle three times, well composed;
with fourfold force, sounding with the whole army. Having done thus he should go home, having released the water-handful;
this peace called Nirajana is for growth and crushes enemies.
Their sons and grandsons took refuge in eight forces: Bhadra, Manda, Mriga, Gaja and Sankirna —
born in forest after forest, those great elephants, source of Kama. May the Vasus, Rudras, Adityas and hosts of Maruts protect you;
protect your master, lord of elephants; let the agreement be kept. Mounted on Airavata, thunderbolt in hand, Shatakratu,
following behind, may that king of gods protect you. Gain victory in battle and go always secure;
gain strength like Airavata in battle. Prosperity from the Moon, strength from Vishnu, splendor from the Sun, speed from the wind,
steadiness from the mountain, victory from Rudra, fame from the god Purandara. May the elephants and the directions with deities protect you in battle;
may the Ashvins with Gandharvas protect you from all directions; Manus, Vasus, Rudras, Vayu, Soma, great sages,
hosts of nagas, kinnaras, gandharvas, yakshas, spirits, planets, Pramathas with the Adityas, the Lord of beings with the Mothers,
Indra, the commander Skanda and Varuna rest on you. May they burn all enemies; may the king attain victory.
Whatever ornaments employed by enemies all around, may they fall, struck by your splendor, of your enemies.
As in the killing of Kalanemi, in battle at the destruction of Tripura, in the war and death of Hiranyakashipu, and among all demons,
so you are glorious today; shine, remember the covenant. Seeing this blue-white one, may the king's enemies quickly perish,
conquered in battle by various terrible diseases and weapons. Putana, Revati, Lekha, Kalaratri are recited:
may they burn quickly all enemies, resting on you, O banner. In the great Sarvamedha sacrifice by the god of gods, the trident-bearer,
by Sharva, and from the essence of the world you were fashioned. Remember Nandaka's other form, destroyer of enemies;
dark as a blue-lotus petal, Krishna, destroyer of bad dreams: Asi, Vishasana, Khadga, Tikshnadhara, Durasada,
Augarbha, Vijaya and Dharmapala — these eight names of yours were told earlier by the Self-born.
Your star is Krittika; your teacher is the god Maheshvara; gold is your body; your deity is Janardana.
Sword, protect the king with his army and city; father, grandfather, god — you protect always.
Armor, you give welfare in battle; today may fame be mine in the army; protect me, who am to be protected; sinless one, homage to you.
Drum, you who shake the hearts of rivals by your sound, be for the earth's armies the increaser of victory;
as the best elephants rejoice at a cloud's roar, so may our joy, bringing delight, come from your sound.
As terror arises in women from a cloud's sound, so by your sound may our enemies tremble in battle.
With mantras they should always be worshipped, to be used in victories and the like. A ghee-blanket for Vishnu and others, and a consecration at the year's end —
the king's consecration should be done by the astrologer-priest.
Hrishikesha in the corners, Janardana in their gaps, Hari in boar form on the ground, Narasimha in the sky is mine.
This stainless, razor-edged wheel, Sudarshana, whirls; its garland of rays is hard to look at, to kill ghosts and night-wanderers.
This mace, shining like a blazing fire of a thousand flames, destroys demons, spirits, pishachas and dakinis.
May the twang of Vasudeva's Sarnga bow destroy my enemies, animals, men, kushmandas, ghosts and the rest, entirely.
Those who are gathered, thrown off by the sword's edge and shining moonlight — may they go and be pacified at once, like snakes by Garuda.
Kushmandas, yakshas, daityas, night-wanderers, ghosts, cruel Vinayakas, humans, jambhagas, birds,
lions and the like, animals, biting serpents — may they all become gentle, struck by the sound of Krishna's conch.
Those who steal the movements of my mind, those who steal memory, those who steal strength and vigor, and those who corrupt the shadow,
those who steal enjoyments and those who destroy auspicious marks — may those Kushmandas perish, struck by the sound of Vishnu's discus.
May health of intellect, health of mind and health of senses be mine by the praise of the god of gods, Vasudeva.
May Janardana Hari be behind and before me, south and north, and in the corners. One who has bowed to him, the praiseworthy lord, infinite, Achyuta, Janardana, does not sink.
As Hari is supreme Brahman and the beyond, and that same Keshava is the form of the world — by that truth, by reciting Achyuta's name may he quickly destroy my threefold evil.
Only twenty-five here are declared the Sama measure. Sumantu, Jajali and Shlokayani in the Atharva;
Shaunaka, Pippalada, Munjakesha and others; ten thousand mantras, sixty hundred, and a hundred Upanishads.
That Lord in the form of Vyasa had the divisions of the branches made. After the divisions of branches, Vishnu is the history and the Purana.
Having received the Puranas and the rest from Vyasa, Suta Lomaharshana; and Sumati, Agnivarchas, Mitrayu, Shimshapayana,
Kritavrata and Savarni — six were his disciples. Shamshapayana and the rest made the compilations of the Puranas.
